prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one 16:9 cinematic visual-development frame for an AI brand short shown at a professional industry event. This is a proposal, no typography.
Input images: image 1 ONLY defines the identity and shapes of Chacha, image 2 ONLY defines identity and shapes of Chamei. These are NOT render-style references. Translate the character shapes into unmistakably volumetric 3D cinema characters with visible side planes, foreshortened limbs, three-dimensional cast shadows and perspective. Do NOT copy the flat reference illustration render or layout.
Exactly two characters: Chacha on left, broad rounded WHITE face with tiny rounded ears, small simple black eyes, black nose and little expressive mouth, squat compact body, mint-green T-shirt, large white tail with TWO black elongated marks. Keep its broad cheek silhouette, not a generic cat or bear; no whiskers or long muzzle. Chamei on right wears orange bear-ear hood with tiny bear face on it, brown fringe and side locks, warm pale face, rosy cheek patches, simple small dark oval eyes, round hands. Keep canonical upper-body proportions, waist-up framing, no newly invented lower-body costume. Chamei remains a stylized CG character, not a real child. No giant human eyes, no realistic skin pores.
Action and layout: the two characters are ACTIVELY cooperating at a model-capability workbench rather than presenting to camera. Chacha leans in from left, pushing one large mint connector plug forward toward the central socket; Chamei on right holds the receiving module steady, concentrating with an amused, knowing expression. Three clearly separate palm-sized capability modules sit along a diagonal work surface, with simple icons for picture, audio and text. Their operation is a visual metaphor, no actual API or UI claimed. Capture the instant just before connector slots in. Characters look at the task and each other, not at viewer. Poses must feel alive, asymmetrical and physically weighted.
Camera/composition: dynamic slightly low 35mm cinema lens, medium two-shot in three-quarter perspective, counter runs diagonally through frame. Both faces sharp, clear depth from foreground plug to characters to background. Strong main action readable on a large event screen. Background is a streamlined creative-tech workshop with architectural frames and one large rear window, no decorative plant clutter. Leave controlled breathing room around head silhouettes.
Palette: mint/emerald and charcoal, warm cream, character orange and a small warm-yellow light accent. Natural white Chacha face preserved even in shadow. Bright-enough face lighting, deeper shadows and purposeful contrast, not pastel nursery. No words, logos, captions, watermark, reference sheet or panels. NO fluffy fur, plush toys, felt dolls, infant proportions, glossy collectible figurines, paper cutouts, photoreal human skin, gratuitous neon or cyberpunk city.
Style/medium: a bold contemporary COMIC-CINEMA 3D animation still. The underlying character sculpture must read as solid dimensional 3D; use directional sculpting light, stylized two-to-three-level shadow bands and selective tapered ink contours. Surfaces are smooth graphic CG with NO fuzz or fabric pile. Shirt/hood have a few simplified purposeful modeled folds. Restrained halftone dots ONLY inside selected dark shadow regions, not all over the image. Fine hand-inked accent lines describe cheek and cloth curvature. Clean broad shapes, striking asymmetrical cinematic framing, strong silhouette staging.
Lighting: bright warm directional key from upper left, controlled emerald bounce from the workbench, dark charcoal falloff for contrast, crisp cream rim separation. Camera depth and modeled objects remain apparent despite cel-like shadow design. Add just ONE short graphic speed stroke behind the moving plug and a tiny two-line reaction accent near Chamei, with no text. Energetic witty grown-up animated comedy, not a flat comic panel and not a toy product photograph.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Edit target: first reference image is an already generated fully volumetric 3D scene with the white green-shirt mascot left, orange bear-hood character right, and a capability workbench. KEEP EXACT character identities, silhouettes, poses, camera, counter geometry, plug, modules, icon positions and composition. Change ONLY the render treatment, light-shape design, and surface textures.
This is a strong NON-PHOTOREALISTIC COMIC-CINEMA restyle, not a subtle color grade. The current image is too soft, fabric-textured and toy-like.
MANDATORY visible transformation across the whole image:
1. Remove ALL plush, fur, fuzzy cloth and pebbled toy microtexture. Characters have clean sculpted 3D volumes with flat graphic albedo.
2. Replace soft rounded gradient shading with distinct hard-edged two- or three-tone shadow regions that wrap around the modeled cheeks, hands, hood and clothes. Keep a clear light side, shadow side and small rim edge on each character so they remain obviously 3D, never flat paper cutouts.
3. Add clean selective dark ink contours to silhouettes and folds, tapered lines with strong graphic control; dark mint/charcoal lines rather than thick toddler crayon scribble.
4. Add restrained coarse comic halftone dots INSIDE dark shadow regions only, especially beneath the hood and on the table. Some hand-drawn hatch accents on background forms.
5. Use crisp ivory highlights and deep emerald shadows, flatter color planes on architecture, one controlled warm-orange key light. No bloom, no photoreal fabric shaders, no pastel haze.
6. Add three elegant graphic speed strokes trailing the connector to clarify motion, no words or labels. Maintain character eye direction toward the operation, NOT toward viewer.
Visual target: bold stylized 3D animation rendered as moving graphic-novel cinema. Aggressive enough graphic treatment that it could not be mistaken for the original smooth toy render. Keep warm white mascot face, mint shirt, orange hood and black facial features. No text, no logos, no watermark. Single 16:9 image.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: single 16:9 concept frame testing COMIC-CINEMA 3D CHARACTERS combined with PREMIUM TECHNOLOGY PRODUCT 3D ENVIRONMENT.
Input image 1 is the exact edit target and character/render reference. KEEP the two characters IDENTICAL: same face shapes, relative size, orange hood, mint shirt, tail markings, hands, poses, eye directions, confident ink contours, hard-edged cel shadow bands and small halftone shadow accents. Preserve the dynamic low-camera three-quarter view, medium two-shot, positions of the plug and all capability modules, and their icon identities. Chacha is pushing the connector, Chamei braces the receiving module. Do not alter their expression or revert to plush/fur/soft-toy characters.
Change ONLY the workshop environment, table design and prop materials to a restrained high-end technology product demonstration stage:
- Replace the cluttered warm wooden workshop, window and blackboard with a carefully composed warm-ivory architectural cyclorama containing two large vertical frosted-glass planes, a single deep-emerald structural arc and quiet negative space. No literal office furniture or decorative plants.
- Work surface becomes satin charcoal anodized aluminum with very subtle edge highlights and a narrow glass inset; no circuitry carpet or spaceship console.
- Capability modules retain their exact silhouettes/icons/locations but use accurately machined metal outer shells, satin ceramic corner pieces and translucent pale-mint glass faces with physically plausible reflections and refraction. Preserve three simple image/audio/text icons; central connector is an abstract matching interface, not a real electrical product specification.
- Let a SINGLE thin mint light trace on the worktop connect the module bases to visually express a common system. No beams, floating holograms, generic neon sci-fi, excess gadgets, numbers or text.
Cohesion: characters remain selectively inked and cel-shaded 3D; PRODUCT OBJECTS and SET have realistic precise material response. Their camera perspective, illumination direction, contact shadows, overlap and reflected green bounce must all match. Keep the warm key from upper left and neutral fill; reduce overall orange background saturation because the orange hood is the focal accent. Characters cast believable shadows onto the realistic stage; their hands actually meet the plug/module. Keep both faces bright and readable, use controlled green specular accents rather than everywhere-glowing edges.
Goal: intentionally designed mixed rendering that feels like one animated film shot, active characters operating tangible product objects. Visually clean, grown-up technology-brand aesthetic with comic performance. Not a flat sticker pasted onto a photograph. No labels, subtitles, fake brand logos, watermark, extra characters or panels.
